attributes.nuance_translation: A structure that highlights that just with (A), (B) may be expected, or is only natural.

attributes.body_ja:
「だけに」は「(A) だからこそ、当然（とうぜん） (B) になる」や「(A) から期待（きたい）される通（とお）りに (B) だ」といった意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）す表現（ひょうげん）です。これは「だけ」に「に」が付（つ）いてできています。

「だけに」は、(A) という理由（りゆう）や状況（じょうきょう）からもたらされた結果（けっか）が、良（よ）い場合（ばあい）にも悪（わる）い場合（ばあい）にも使（つか）われます。動詞（どうし）、イ形容詞（けいようし）、「な」を伴（ともな）うナ形容詞（けいようし）、または名詞（めいし）の後（あと）に付（つ）きます。

また「だけに」は「(A) なので、その分（ぶん）もっと (B) だ」といったニュアンスで使（つか）われることもあります。この場合（ばあい）、難（むずか）しさのレベル、感情（かんじょう）の強（つよ）さ、量（りょう）などについて、(B) が予想（よそう）や期待（きたい）を超（こ）えて大（おお）きくなる場合（ばあい）に使（つか）われます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「だけに」は、どちらの意味（いみ）で使（つか）われる場合（ばあい）でも共通（きょうつう）して、聞（き）き手（て）の注意（ちゅうい）をまず (A) に向（む）け、「だからこそ (B) なのだ」とその重要性（じゅうようせい）を強調（きょうちょう）する働（はたら）きを持（も）っています。
attributes.body:
だけに is a grammar pattern that is often translated as 'as might be expected of (A)', 'it's only natural due to (A)', or simply 'because of (A)'. Being a combination of だけ 'just', and に 'to', the literal meaning is 'just in that it's (A)', and is similar to the counterpart phrase in English.

だけに may be used when highlighting either positive or negative results that came about due to (A), and will appear after verbs, い-Adjectives, な-Adjectives that have been followed by な, or nouns.

Also, だけに may be used when highlighting that specifically because of (A), (B) is considered a level above what would usually be expected. This can be in terms of difficulty, emotional reaction, volume, or anything else that is quantifiable.

Fun-fact

With any of these meanings, the equivalent 'just in that it's (A)' English expression can be utilized as an accurate interpretation, as both it and だけに often just draw the listener's attention to (A), in order to show that (B) is noteworthy because of it.

attributes.source: [DAJG] A Dictionary of Advanced Japanese Grammar

だけに vs. だけあって
〜だけに・〜だけあって breakdown and examples

attributes.body: Both mean as might be expected. だけあって usually leads to a positive evaluation, as in 有名なだけあって味は素晴らしい (As expected of a famous restaurant, the taste is excellent). だけに can be positive or negative, often stressing proportionality, as in 苦労しただけに喜びも大きい (Because I struggled, the joy is even greater).

second_relatable.title: だけに

attributes.body: Both だけに and わけだ can be used to draw conclusions, but differ in tone and focus. だけに emphasizes an expected result based on a known condition, e.g. 忙しい人だけに来ないと思った ('Precisely because he's a busy man, I thought he wouldn't come'), while わけだ indicates the speaker's realization based on something previously expressed or observed, e.g. だから来ないわけだ ('So that's why he's not coming').

second_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

attributes.body: Both imply results in line with expectations. だけのことはある expresses admiration, always at sentence-end, as in 練習しただけのことはあって優勝した (He won, as you’d expect from his practice). だけに is more flexible, attaching to another phrase that states the result, and can be used positively or negatively.
